A goal is a wish with a plan and a deadline. “I want a bike” is a wish. “I'll save up for a bike by summer” is already a goal!
Which of these is a goal?
10 push-ups every day until the end of the month
It would be great to go to the sea
It says what to do and by when. That's what turns a wish into a goal.
A good goal has three things: what exactly, how much and by what day. Try to come up with your own!
A big dream is scary to start. So it's cut into steps, like a pizza into slices.
Dream: learn to swim. Which first step is best?
Swim across a river right away
Sign up for a pool and go for the first time
Wait until it happens by itself
A small step you can take this very week.
Every step done is a reason to celebrate. In “Dreams” every goal has its own steps.
Sometimes a step doesn't work out. That's normal, even for grown-ups! The main thing is not to give up, but to change the plan a little.
You wanted to read for 20 minutes but didn't have time. What's better?
Read for 10 minutes tomorrow, but for sure
A little less, but every day — that's how goals are reached.
A month is a handy deadline: long enough to make it, short enough not to forget.
Get at least a B in math on 4 tests
It can be checked: it's clear what exactly, how much and when.
Write your goal for the month in “Dreams” and split it into weekly steps.
“Need” — you can't do without it: food, clothes, textbooks. “Want” — something nice, but you can live without it.
Winter boots when the old ones are too small are a…
Without them it's cold, so it's a need.
A fifth toy car for the collection is a…
Nice, but you can do without it. Wanting is normal, it's just important to tell the difference.
Write everything you want into the wish jar: big and small. A written wish won't be forgotten.
Once a week I'll ask which wish you want to turn into a goal. Then we'll come up with steps together.
Where to keep wishes so you don't forget?
Your head is for ideas, and what's written down isn't lost.
Here's a trick: want to buy something — wait 3 days. If you still want it just as much, you really need it.
You saw a new toy and really want it. What should you do?
Spend all your money right away
Write it in the wish jar and wait 3 days
Often after 3 days you want something else, and the money is still safe.
Mom, dad, your brother or sister have dreams too. Finding them out and helping is really cool.
How do you find out what mom dreams of?
Ask, and your gift will hit the mark.
Money appears when people do useful work: heal, teach, build, sell houses.
How can you earn money yourself?
Do a useful chore agreed with your parents
Smart people don't spend everything at once. They split money into three jars: Spend, Save and Share.
Grandma gave you 100 coins. Split them between the jars — tap the jars!
Your pocket money is split automatically the way you agreed with your parents.
A bike costs 4,500. If you save 500 a week, how many weeks will you wait?
4,500 ÷ 500 = 9. The more you save, the sooner the dream.
In “Dreams” you can see how much is saved and how much is left.
The “Share” jar is for gifts to loved ones and helping those in need. Giving feels good!
Gifts and help — that's exactly what “Share” is.
A budget is a plan: how much money comes in and where it goes. Grown-ups do this every month.
Pocket money is 500 a week, 40% goes to “Save”. How much is that?
If you put money in a bank, the bank pays you interest. Ask your parents for more — it's an interesting topic!
